claim: Tim29 (C19orf52) is a novel, metazoan-specific subunit of the human TIM22 complex.
source: Here, we identify Tim29 (C19orf52) as a novel, metazoan-specific subunit of the human TIM22 complex.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Tim29 is integrated into the mitochondrial inner membrane with its C-terminus exposed to the intermembrane space.
source: The protein is integrated into the mitochondrial inner membrane with it's C-terminus exposed to the intermembrane space.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, which is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Tim29 is required for the stability of the TIM22 complex.
source: Tim29 is required for the stability of the TIM22 complex and functions in the assembly of hTim22.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, supported by knockdown experiments shown in Figures 4 and 6.

claim: Tim29 functions in the assembly of hTim22.
source: Tim29 is required for the stability of the TIM22 complex and functions in the assembly of hTim22.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, supported by import and assembly experiments in Figure 6.

claim: Tim29 contacts the Translocase of the Outer Mitochondrial Membrane (TOM complex).
source: Furthermore, Tim29 contacts the Translocase of the Outer Mitochondrial Membrane, TOM complex, enabling a mechanism for transport of hydrophobic carrier substrates across the aqueous intermembrane space.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by immunoprecipitation and crosslinking experiments in Figures 8 and 9.

claim: The TIM22 complex mediates the import of hydrophobic carrier proteins into the mitochondrial inner membrane.
source: The TIM22 complex mediates the import of hydrophobic carrier proteins into the mitochondrial inner membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about the TIM22 complex.

claim: The human TIM22 complex remains poorly characterised compared to the yeast complex.
source: While the TIM22 machinery has been well characterised in yeast, the human complex remains poorly characterised.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as motivation for the study.

claim: Mitochondria contain approximately 1500 different proteins.
source: This genesis requires the ~1500 different mitochondrial proteins to be imported via dynamic translocation machines to one of four subcompartments of the organelle – outer and inner membrane, intermembrane space and matrix (Chacinska et al., 2009; Stojanovski et al., 2012; Dolezal et al., 2006; Harbauer et al., 2014; Neupert and Herrmann, 2007; Baker et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The TOM complex is the general entry gate to mitochondria.
source: The Translocase of the Outer Membrane (TOM) complex is described as the general entry gate to mitochondria and provides a passageway through which precursors can cross the outer membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: The TIM23 complex typically transports proteins that possess a matrix-targeting N-terminal presequence.
source: The TIM23 complex typically transports proteins that possess a matrix-targeting N-terminal presequence (Chacinska et al., 2009; Neupert and Herrmann, 2007; Wagner et al., 2009; Mokranjac and Neupert, 2010)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The TIM22 complex mediates the inner membrane insertion of multi-transmembrane spanning proteins that contain internal targeting elements.
source: while the TIM22 complex mediates the inner membrane insertion of multi-transmembrane spanning proteins that contain internal targeting elements (Chacinska et al., 2009; Neupert and Herrmann, 2007; Rehling et al., 2004; Koehler, 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Substrates of the TIM22 complex include the mitochondrial carrier family, such as the ADP/ATP carrier (AAC) and the phosphate carrier (PiC).
source: Substrates of the TIM22 complex include the mitochondrial carrier family, such as the ADP/ATP carrier (AAC) and the phosphate carrier (PiC), and multispanning inner membrane proteins like, Tim17 and Tim23 (subunits of the TIM23 complex) and Tim22 itself (pore forming unit of the TIM22 complex) (Chacinska et al., 2009; Stojanovski et al., 2012; Koehler, 2004; Sirrenberg et al., 1996; Káldi et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: In yeast cells, TIM22 is a 300-kDa complex consisting of four membrane integral subunits: Tim22, Tim54, Tim18 and Sdh3.
source: In yeast cells, TIM22 is a 300-kDa complex, consisting of four membrane integral subunits, Tim22, Tim54, Tim18 and Sdh3, and a peripheral chaperone complex consisting of the small TIM proteins, Tim9-Tim10-Tim12 (Adam et al., 1999; Gebert et al., 2011; Jarosch et al., 1997, 1996; Kerscher et al., 1997, 2000; Koehler et al., 2000, 1998; Kovermann et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The yeast TIM22 complex includes a peripheral chaperone complex consisting of the small TIM proteins Tim9-Tim10-Tim12.
source: In yeast cells, TIM22 is a 300-kDa complex, consisting of four membrane integral subunits, Tim22, Tim54, Tim18 and Sdh3, and a peripheral chaperone complex consisting of the small TIM proteins, Tim9-Tim10-Tim12 (Adam et al., 1999; Gebert et al., 2011; Jarosch et al., 1997, 1996; Kerscher et al., 1997, 2000; Koehler et al., 2000, 1998; Kovermann et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Small TIM proteins are a family of intermembrane space chaperones that facilitate the passage of hydrophobic membrane proteins through the aqueous environment.
source: The small TIM proteins are a family of intermembrane space chaperones that facilitate the passage of hydrophobic membrane proteins through this aqueous environment.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Tim9 and Tim10 form a soluble hexameric complex.
source: Tim9 and Tim10 form a soluble hexameric complex, but a fraction also interacts with the TIM22 complex via assembly with Tim12 (Adam et al., 1999; Gebert et al., 2008; Baud et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The human TIM22 complex consists of hTim22, hTim9, hTim10a, and hTim10b.
source: Like yeast, the human TIM22 complex consists of the channel-forming hTim22 protein, along with subunits of the small TIM family, hTim9, hTim10a, and hTim10b (Mühlenbein et al., 2004)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: hTim10b is the functional homologue of yeast Tim12.
source: with hTim10b being the functional homologue of yeast Tim12 (Koehler et al., 1998; Baud et al., 2007; Mühlenbein et al., 2004; Gentle et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Homologues of yeast Tim54 or Tim18 are absent in human cells.
source: However, homologues of yeast Tim54 or Tim18 are absent in human cells and there is no evidence to indicate that the Sdh3 homologue, SDHC, interacts with the human TIM22 translocase.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: There is no evidence that the Sdh3 homologue, SDHC, interacts with the human TIM22 translocase.
source: However, homologues of yeast Tim54 or Tim18 are absent in human cells and there is no evidence to indicate that the Sdh3 homologue, SDHC, interacts with the human TIM22 translocase.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: hTim10b3XFLAG was exclusively localised to mitochondria when assessed by fluorescence microscopy.
source: The FLAG-tagged protein was exclusively localised to mitochondria when assessed by fluorescence microscopy (Figure 1A, upper panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: hTim10b3XFLAG formed the same assemblies as untagged hTim10b protein, including the hTim9-hTim10a-hTim10b hexamer and a 450-kDa TIM22 complex.
source: Blue Native (BN)-PAGE of isolated mitochondria revealed that hTim10b3XFLAG formed the same assemblies as the untagged hTim10b protein (assessed by in vitro import of hTim10b into isolated mitochondria), including the hTim9-hTim10a-hTim10b hexamer and a higher molecular weight 450-kDa TIM22 complex (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: Known interacting partners hTim10a, hTim9 and hTim22 co-purified specifically with hTim10b3XFLAG.
source: Among proteins that co-purified specifically with hTim10b3XFLAG were known interacting partners hTim10a, hTim9 and hTim22 (Figure 1E and Figure 1—source data 1)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: C19orf52 displayed significant enrichment in the hTim10b3XFLAG sample.
source: The uncharacterised protein, C19orf52, also displayed significant enrichment in the hTim10b3XFLAG sample (Figure 1E and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Sequence similarity searches for C19orf52 did not reveal homologs in lower eukaryotes.
source: Sequence similarity searches for C19orf52 did not reveal homologs in lower eukaryotes.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: C19orf52 is conserved in metazoan species.
source: However, C19orf52 is conserved in metazoan species (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: C19orf52 is predicted to possess an N-terminal presequence at amino acids 1–16.
source: The previously uncharacterised protein is predicted to possess an N-terminal presequence at amino acids 1–16, based on the MitoProt II bioinformatics program (Claros, 1995; Claros and Vincens, 1996)
evidence: This is stated in the results based on bioinformatics prediction.

claim: C19orf52 is predicted to possess a single transmembrane domain spanning amino acids 61–79.
source: and a single transmembrane domain spanning amino acids 61–79 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: C19orf52 could be imported into mitochondria in a time-dependent manner.
source: C19orf52 could be imported into a protease-protected location and in a time-dependent manner, but we did not observe proteolytic processing of the protein (Figure 2B, upper panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Proteolytic processing of C19orf52 was not observed during import.
source: C19orf52 could be imported into a protease-protected location and in a time-dependent manner, but we did not observe proteolytic processing of the protein (Figure 2B, upper panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The import of C19orf52 was inhibited under conditions where the membrane potential had been dissipated.
source: However, the import of C19orf52 was inhibited under conditions where the membrane potential (Δψ) had been dissipated (Figure 2B, upper panel, lane 8)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: C19orf52 import occurs via a membrane potential-dependent import pathway.
source: in a similar manner to pOTC (Figure 2B, lower panel, lane 8), suggesting import via a Δψ-dependent import pathway.
evidence: This is stated in the results based on experimental data in Figure 2B.

claim: Full length C19orf52 showed exclusive localisation to mitochondria.
source: C19orf52 showed exclusive localisation to mitochondria (Figure 2C, upper panel), confirming the protein is indeed mitochondrial.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: C19orf52Δ16 and C19orf52aa17-89, which both lack the N-terminal 16 amino acids, were both targeted to mitochondria.
source: C19orf52Δ16 and C19orf52aa17-89, which both lack the N-terminal 16 amino acids were both targeted to mitochondria, suggesting that residues 1–16 are dispensable for targeting to the organelle (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: C19orf52aa1-89 displayed exclusive mitochondrial localisation.
source: Expression of C19orf52aa1-89 also displayed exclusive mitochondrial localisation, while C19orf52aa80-260 could not be targeted to mitochondria and was localised to the cytosol (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: C19orf52aa80-260 could not be targeted to mitochondria and was localised to the cytosol.
source: Expression of C19orf52aa1-89 also displayed exclusive mitochondrial localisation, while C19orf52aa80-260 could not be targeted to mitochondria and was localised to the cytosol (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: C19orf523XFLAG was present in isolated mitochondria and only became accessible to external protease when the outer membrane was disrupted.
source: C19orf523XFLAG was present in isolated mitochondria and only became accessible to external protease when the outer membrane was disrupted (Figure 2D, compare lanes 2 and 4), indicating the C-terminal FLAG tag is exposed to the intermembrane space.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The C-terminal FLAG tag of C19orf523XFLAG is exposed to the intermembrane space.
source: C19orf523XFLAG was present in isolated mitochondria and only became accessible to external protease when the outer membrane was disrupted (Figure 2D, compare lanes 2 and 4), indicating the C-terminal FLAG tag is exposed to the intermembrane space.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: C19orf523XFLAG was resistant to carbonate treatment, indicating it is likely an integral membrane protein.
source: C19orf523XFLAG was resistant to carbonate treatment, like the membrane integrated Bak and Mfn2, indicating that it is likely an integral membrane protein (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: C19orf52 is an integral inner membrane protein with a C-terminal domain exposed to the intermembrane space.
source: Taken together this data indicates that C19orf52 is an integral inner membrane protein with a C-terminal domain exposed to the intermembrane space.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: C19orf52△16 and C19orf5217-89 failed to sort properly to the inner membrane and appeared trapped in the outer membrane.
source: Surprisingly, upon subfractionation and carbonate extraction of mitochondria isolated from cells expressing C19orf52△16 and C19orf5217-89 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D) we noticed that these proteins failed to sort properly to the inner membrane, but appeared trapped in the outer membrane, most likely in the TOM complex (indicated by accessibility to protease and presence in both the pellet and supernatant fractions upon carbonate treatment).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The first 16 amino acids of C19orf52 are crucial for subsequent sorting to the inner membrane.
source: Thus, although the first 16 amino acids originally appeared to be dispensable for mitochondrial targeting, closer examination revealed that these residues are indeed crucial for subsequent sorting of C19orf52 to the inner membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: C19orf52 specific antibodies revealed the presence of a high molecular weight complex of approximately 450-kDa.
source: C19orf52 specific antibodies revealed the presence of a high molecular weight complex of approximately 450-kDa, reminiscent of the TIM22 complex in both control (Figure 3A, lane 1) and hTim10b3XFLAG mitochondria (Figure 3A, lane 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A slight delay in the migration of the C19orf52-containing complex was observed in mitochondria isolated from hTim10b3XFLAG expressing cells.
source: We observed a slight delay in the migration of the C19orf52-containing complex in mitochondria isolated from hTim10b3XFLAG expressing cells (Figure 3A, lane 2 and 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: C19orf52 is located within a hTim10b3XFLAG-containing complex.
source: This suggested that C19orf52 is located within a hTim10b3XFLAG-containing complex and the presence of the FLAG-tag is causing the observed delay in mobility.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the experimental data.

claim: FLAG antibodies shifted [35S]-hTim22 (hTIM22 complex) in both hTim10b3XFLAG and C19orf523XFLAG containing mitochondria.
source: As can be seen (Figure 3B, lanes 2, and 8), the FLAG antibodies shifted [35S]-hTim22 (hTIM22 complex) in both hTim10b3XFLAG and C19orf523XFLAG containing mitochondria, suggesting the presence of all three proteins within the same complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: C19orf523XFLAG specifically immunoprecipitated hTim22.
source: In an alternative approach C19orf523XFLAG was shown to specifically immunoprecipitate hTim22 (Figure 3C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: C19orf52 could be co-immunoprecipitated with hTim10b3XFLAG.
source: while C19orf52 could be co-immunoprecipitated with hTim10b3XFLAG (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Immunoprecipitation of C19orf523XFLAG and subsequent quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics analysis revealed the presence of all known TIM22 complex subunits.
source: As a final source of confirmation immunoprecipitation of C19orf523XFLAG and subsequent quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics analysis revealed the presence of all known TIM22 complex subunits, including hTim22, hTim10b, hTim10a and hTim9 (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to mass spectrometry data.

claim: C19orf52 is a bona fide subunit of the human TIM22 complex.
source: These findings confirm that C19orf52 is a bona fide subunit of the human TIM22 complex, and represents a novel metazoan specific subunit of the translocation machine.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: C19orf52 represents a novel metazoan specific subunit of the TIM22 translocation machine.
source: These findings confirm that C19orf52 is a bona fide subunit of the human TIM22 complex, and represents a novel metazoan specific subunit of the translocation machine.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The protein C19orf52 is renamed as Tim29.
source: Given that the molecular weight of the protein is 29 kDa and the nomenclature of the mitochondrial protein import machinery (Pfanner et al., 1996), we henceforth rename this protein as Tim29 and its gene as TIMM29.
evidence: This is stated in the results with citation to nomenclature conventions.

claim: Knockdown of Tim29 significantly reduced basal mitochondrial oxygen consumption to 65%.
source: Knockdown of Tim29 significantly reduced basal mitochondrial oxygen consumption to 65% (p<0.05) compared to cells transfected with a control scrambled siRNA (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Knockdown of hTim22 reduced basal mitochondrial oxygen consumption to 61%.
source: This reduction in basal oxygen consumption was similar to that observed in hTim22 KD cells (61% residual respiration, p<0.05).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate was significantly lower in Tim29 KD cells compared to control cells (88% residual respiration).
source: Following addition of FCCP, the maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate was also significantly lower in Tim29 KD cells compared to control cells (88% residual respiration, p<0.05)
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: The maximal mitochondrial oxygen consumption rate in hTim22 knockdown cells was 63% compared to control.
source: and in hTim22 knockdown cells compared to the control (63%, p<0.05).
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: KD of both Tim29 and hTim22 did not have any significant impact on cell proliferation.
source: KD of both Tim29 and hTim22 did not have any significant impact on cell proliferation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), or cell viability (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: KD of both Tim29 and hTim22 did not have any significant impact on cell viability.
source: KD of both Tim29 and hTim22 did not have any significant impact on cell proliferation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), or cell viability (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Specific depletion of TIM22 complex substrates, including hTim23, ANT3 and the glutamate carrier was observed in both Tim29 and hTim22 depleted mitochondria.
source: Specific depletion of TIM22 complex substrates, including hTim23, ANT3 and the glutamate carrier was observed in both Tim29 and hTim22 depleted mitochondria (quantifications shown in Figure 4A and B, lower panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: The depletion of Tim29 led to a significant reduction in the levels of hTim22.
source: The depletion of Tim29 also led to a significant reduction in the levels of hTim22 (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The lack of hTim22 had no obvious effect on the levels of Tim29.
source: while the lack of hTim22 had no obvious effect on the levels of Tim29, indicating Tim29 is imported in a TIM22-independent manner (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Tim29 is imported in a TIM22-independent manner.
source: while the lack of hTim22 had no obvious effect on the levels of Tim29, indicating Tim29 is imported in a TIM22-independent manner (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the experimental data in Figure 4B.

claim: Depletion of Tim29 caused a reduction in the assembly of ANT3 and hTIM23 complexes.
source: BN-PAGE analysis also revealed that depletion of Tim29 caused a reduction in the assembly of ANT3 and hTIM23 complexes (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Reduction in hTIM23 complex caused a reduction in the steady state level of TIM23 complex substrates (COXIV, NDUFV2 and NDUFV1).
source: with the latter causing a reduction in the steady state level of TIM23 complex substrates (COXIV, NDUFV2 and NDUFV1) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The decrease in Tim29 protein levels revealed a reduction in the levels of the endogenous TIM22 complex on BN-PAGE.
source: The decrease in Tim29 protein levels also revealed a reduction in the levels of the endogenous TIM22 complex on BN-PAGE (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The assembly of ANT1 proceeded like WT in the absence of Tim29.
source: While the assembly of ANT1 was reduced in the absence of hTim22 at 60 min (Figure 5A; right panel), assembly of the protein proceeded like WT in the absence of Tim29 (Figure 5A; left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The assembly of ANT1 was reduced in the absence of hTim22 at 60 min.
source: While the assembly of ANT1 was reduced in the absence of hTim22 at 60 min (Figure 5A; right panel), assembly of the protein proceeded like WT in the absence of Tim29 (Figure 5A; left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The assembly of hTim23 was mildly reduced in mitochondria depleted of either Tim29 or hTim22.
source: In contrast, the assembly of hTim23 was mildly reduced in mitochondria depleted of either Tim29 or hTim22 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was a clear assembly defect of [35S]-hTim22 into the TIM22 complex in mitochondria isolated from Tim29 KD cells.
source: In mitochondria isolated from control cells, [35S]-hTim22 efficiently assembled into the 450-kDa TIM22 complex (Figure 6A and B, lanes 1–4), while there was a clear assembly defect into the TIM22 complex in mitochondria isolated from Tim29 KD cells (Figure 6A, lanes 5–8).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The amount of assembled TIM22 complex in Tim29 KD mitochondria was lower than that in the control mitochondria by 53%, after a 60 min-import.
source: The amount of assembled TIM22 complex in Tim29 KD mitochondria was lower than that in the control mitochondria by 53%, after a 60 min-import.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: There was a significant reduction in the assembly of hTim22 into the mature complex in Tim29 KD mitochondria (t[2] = 6.02, p<0.05).
source: To support this observation, we examined the difference in hTim22 protein assembly in control and Tim29 KD mitochondria using a two-tailed Student's t-test. We obtained a t[2] = 6.02 (p<0.05), demonstrating a significant reduction in the assembly of hTim22 into the mature complex in Tim29 KD mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis.

claim: A moderate increase (~20%) in assembled TIM22 complex was consistently detected in hTim22 KD mitochondria after a 60 min-import compared to control mitochondria (t[2] = −5.07, p<0.05).
source: On the contrary, we consistently detected a moderate increase (~20%) in assembled TIM22 complex in hTim22 KD mitochondria after a 60 min-import compared to control mitochondria (t[2] = −5.07, p<0.05).
evidence: This is stated in the results with statistical analysis.

claim: [35S]-hTim22 protein efficiently integrated into the inner membrane in mitochondria isolated from both Tim29 and hTim22 KD cells.
source: In the absence of Tim29 we did observe a minor decrease in the import kinetics of [35S]-hTim22 by SDS-PAGE (Figure 7), however, following treatment of isolated mitochondria with sodium carbonate it was apparent that [35S]-hTim22 protein efficiently integrated into the inner membrane in mitochondria isolated from both Tim29 and hTim22 KD cells (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 7C and 7D.

claim: Tim29 is required for the assembly of the hTim22 protein into the TIM22 complex.
source: Based on these observations, we conclude that Tim29 is required for the assembly of the hTim22 protein into the TIM22 complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: Coupling of the TOM and TIM23 complexes in yeast mitochondria is believed to enhance the import efficiency of presequence-containing precursors.
source: Coupling of the TOM and TIM23 complexes in yeast mitochondria is believed to enhance the import efficiency of presequence-containing precursors (Chacinska et al., 2005, 2003; Waegemann et al., 2015; Mokranjac et al., 2009; Popov-Čeleketić et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Coupling between the TOM and SAM complexes of the outer membrane in yeast mitochondria has been shown to be important for the biogenesis of β-barrel proteins.
source: More recently, coupling between the TOM and SAM complexes of the outer membrane in yeast mitochondria has been shown to be important for the biogenesis of β-barrel proteins (Wenz et al., 2015; Qiu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: No interaction has ever been reported between the TOM and TIM22 translocases in yeast mitochondria.
source: Interestingly, no interaction has ever been reported between the TOM and TIM22 translocases in yeast mitochondria.
evidence: This is stated in the results as established knowledge.

claim: The carrier pathway in yeast is described as a series of five stages, with stage 3 encompassing the transfer of substrates between the TOM and TIM22 complexes by the soluble intermembrane space Tim9-Tim10 complex.
source: Rather, the carrier pathway is described as a series of five stages, with stage 3 encompassing the transfer of substrates between the TOM and TIM22 complexes by the soluble intermembrane space Tim9-Tim10 complex (Chacinska et al., 2009; Rehling et al., 2004; Ryan et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: A fraction of both hTom40 and hTom22 co-eluted with Tim293XFLAG.
source: Interestingly, we observed a fraction of both hTom40 and hTom22 co-eluting with Tim293XFLAG, suggesting a co-operation between Tim29 and the TOM complex (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: A fraction of both hTom40 and hTom22 were observed in the Tim29 elution fraction following import of radiolabelled versions.
source: Indeed a fraction of both hTom40 and hTom22 were observed in the Tim29 elution fraction (Figure 8B, middle and lower panels), like that of the control protein hTim9 (Figure 8B, upper panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: A fraction of hTim9, Tim29 and hTim22 co-purified with the TOM complex when using 3XFLAGhTom22 as bait.
source: We also observed a fraction of hTim9, Tim29 and hTim22 co-purifying with the TOM complex, while numerous controls of the outer membrane (hFis1), intermembrane space (cytochrome c), inner membrane (OPA1, hTim23, Glutamate carrier, COXIV) and matrix (NDUFV1, NDUFV2) did not co-elute with hTom22 (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The interaction between TOM and TIM22 complexes is labile in the absence of precursor protein, or under the conditions employed for the immunoprecipitation.
source: Given that the TIM22 complex was not purified in great amounts, the data suggest the interaction between TOM and TIM22 complexes is labile in the absence of precursor protein, or under the conditions employed for the immunoprecipitation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the experimental data.

claim: hTom40 was found cross-linked to Tim29.
source: Interestingly, we found hTom40 cross-linked to Tim29 (Figure 9A and B), but not hTom22 (Figure 9B, third panel from top).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 9A and 9B.

claim: Crosslinks were observed between Tim29 and hTim9, but not hTim22.
source: We also observed crosslinks between Tim29 and hTim9, but not hTim22 (most likely due to the lack of primary amines in the predicted Tim29 transmembrane domain, which are essential for the amine-reactive crosslinker DSP) (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Cross-links of hTim10b with both hTim9 and Tim29 were observed, but not with hTom40.
source: We next performed cross-linking using mitochondria isolated from cells expressing hTim10b3XFLAG and although we observed cross-links of hTim10b with both hTim9 and Tim29 we did not observe any crosslinks with hTom40 (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Tim29 acts as a bridge between the TIM22 and TOM complexes.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Tim29 acts as a bridge between the TIM22 and TOM complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The number of known subunits of the human TIM22 complex is now five: hTim22, hTim9, hTim10a, hTim10b and Tim29.
source: Our work brings the number of known subunits of the human TIM22 complex to five: hTim22 (Sirrenberg et al., 1996; Bauer et al., 1999), hTim9, hTim10a, hTim10b (Mühlenbein et al., 2004; Gentle et al., 2007; Bauer et al., 1999) and Tim29 (this study).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Immunoprecipitations and mass spectrometry data for both hTim10b3XFLAG and C19orf523XFLAG did not reveal the presence of SDHC.
source: Interestingly, our immunoprecipitations and mass spectrometry data for both hTim10b3XFLAG and C19orf523XFLAG did not reveal the presence of SDHC, suggesting the human protein is not a subunit of the human TIM22 complex, at least under the conditions in which we perform the immunoprecipitation experiments.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The lack of Tim18 in human mitochondria could prevent the association of SDHC to the hTIM22 complex.
source: It is feasible to suggest that the lack of Tim18 in human mitochondria could prevent the association of SDHC to the hTIM22 complex.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as speculation.

claim: Human mitochondria lack soluble Tim9-Tim10 complexes.
